title: Placement-group and PCIe topology impact on decode throughput
content:
Status: working notes / informal experiment log
Owner: Aisha Kumar (eng-serving-runtime)
Summary: quick investigation into how instance placement topology (placement-group / same-host affinity) and PCIe root complex / upstream switch locality affect sustained decode throughput and tail latency for LLM serving. Focused on three representative GPUs (A100, H100, L40S) and two cloud SKU families (dense-gpu and general-purpose GPU), varying driver/CUDA combos as a secondary factor.

Motivation / why we did this
- Observed unexplained throughput oscillations on Dedicated clusters with mixed-placement hosts (tickets linked above).
- Hypothesis: cross-root-complex PCIe hop penalties and multi-socket CPU scheduling cause KV cache warmup jitter and decode throughput degradation for small-batch, long-context workloads.
- We want actionable guidance for Dedicated allocator (prefer same-root placement or require NVLink banding) and conservative defaults for routing.

Experiment matrix (high-level)
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100 (40GB), NVIDIA H100 (80GB), NVIDIA L40S (48GB)
- Cloud SKUs: cg5 (dense-gpu), g5dn (general-purposes with attached GPU), and a competitor region SKU with older PCIe gen
- Placement modes: single-host placement-group (all GPUs on same host), cross-host but same rack (same upstream switch), cross-rack (different leaf/aggregation switch)
- PCIe topologies: direct-root (GPU -> CPU root complex on same CPU socket), cross-socket (GPU associated with other CPU socket via PCIe switch), NVLink presence/absent (where applicable)
- Driver/CUDA: CUDA 12.1 + driver 535, CUDA 12.0 + driver 525 (older), proprietary runtime patches (patched kernel UVM) as X-factor
- Workloads: 1) small-batch decode (batch=1, seq=2048 prefill+decode), 2) medium-batch (batch=4, seq=1024), 3) long-context streaming (seq=32768 with KV-chaining)
- Metrics collected: tokens/sec, decode p50/p90/p99 latency, GPU utilization (sm, pcie util), CPU steal/wait, PCIe Tx/Rx counters, observed stalls (kernel event counters), thermal/power draw, error/retry rate

Methodology details
- Run 10 warmup iterations then 60 measured runs per configuration. Use the serving runtime with identical binary across hosts to avoid software variability.
- Measurement harness: local perf counters + runtime tracing (span-level timestamps for prefill and decode separate). Sync clocks via chrony before each run.
- When testing cross-host, we ensured identical MTU and vNIC config across hosts. We explicitly toggled placement-group & single-host flags provided by the cloud provider.
- For KV-heavy long-context tests, we primed cache with deterministic prefixes to reduce variation from on-the-fly generation.

Selected raw observations (condensed)
- A100, single-host placement-group: baseline for comparison. Small-batch decode tokens/sec = 1450 +/- 2.3% p50; p99 latency stable. PCIe utilization ~12% (prefill heavy).
- A100, cross-host same-rack: tokens/sec dropped ~7% on average; p99 widened by 18% (jitter). Cause points to cross-host network noise and host CPU interrupt handling.
- A100, cross-rack: tokens/sec down ~14%; p99 up ~28%. Observed increased kernel launch stalls aligning with network IRQs during prefill -> decode transition.

- H100, single-host: higher baseline tokens/sec (approx +30% versus A100 for same model/model-size), but more sensitive to cross-socket placement. H100 cross-socket showed 12% throughput drop even for single-host (PCIe root mismatch), with p99 amplification. NVLink presence mitigates this when model fits NVLink partition.

- L40S, single-host: baseline similar to A100 for decode but sustained thermal throttling observed in prolonged long-context tests on some SKUs (likely vendor thermal profile differences). L40S cross-host behavior similar to A100 but SSE stalls different (seen in kernel counters).

- Driver/CUDA effects: newer driver (535) reduced some kernel launch serialization on H100, especially when combined with pinned CPU affinity. Older driver increased the variability across all SKUs by ~3–6% and exacerbated p99s.

Notable micro-correlations
- When GPUs were attached to opposite CPU socket from the process thread (affinity mismatch), we saw additional 4–8% throughput loss and a doubling of p99 jitter for small-batch workloads. Affinity pinning (process -> local CPU) recovered most of that.
- Cross-root-complex PCIe hops introduced measurable stall events in the kernel traces during KV cache population (prefill). These stalls line up with increased PCIe atomic ops and longer DMA completion latencies.
- Placement-group single-host with NVSwitch/NVLink (on H100 hosts) produced the most stable tail latency. When we forced path fallback (disable NVLink), variability rose to levels similar to cross-host.

Representative ASCII table (median numbers across repeated runs, small-batch decode):

GPU  | placement        | tokens/sec | p50ms | p99ms | notes
-----|------------------|------------|-------|-------|----------------------------------------
A100 | single-host      | 1450       | 12.1  | 23.8  | stable baseline
A100 | cross-host rack  | 1250       | 13.6  | 30.6  | network irq coupling observed
H100 | single-host NVL  | 1870       | 9.2   | 18.1  | fastest, low tail
H100 | single-host noNVL| 1650       | 10.8  | 28.9  | p99 worsened without NVLink
L40S | single-host      | 1490       | 11.9  | 26.4  | thermal drift on long-run

Caveats and signal hygiene
- We intentionally did not test cold-cache cold-starts here; this is about sustained decode where KV cache and PCIe patterns dominate.
- Not exhaustive across every cloud SKU; representative SKUs chosen for signal clarity. Individual host firmware/BIOS versions sometimes changed results; we attempted to lock firmware where possible.
- Small absolute differences can matter at scale; even single-digit % throughput changes can translate to large cost deltas on Dedicated.

Interpretation / what this implies for runtime decisions
- Allocation policy: prefer same-host placement for small-batch, long-context workloads. If same-host cannot be guaranteed, prefer hosts with NVLink or explicit same-root PCIe locality.
- CPU pinning: ensure serving worker threads pinned to the CPU socket local to GPU(s) for latency-sensitive routes.
- Driver rollout: test driver 535 (or newer) in a canary pool for H100-heavy clusters; older drivers introduce tail risk.
- Thermal/sku opt-out: for long-context streaming bursts, flag L40S SKU variants with aggressive thermal profiles as "cooldown-sensitive" in Dedicated capacity planning.

Action items / next experiments
- Run focused microbench to quantify PCIe hop cost (measure DMA completion latency distribution) with synthetic kernel that does KV-like scatter/gather. Owner: Marcus Chen, target 2026-03-12.
- Expand matrix to include multi-tenant noise (co-located VMs/GPU workloads) and measure interference amplification. Owner: Elena Park.
- Add an automated placement-group check in the allocator to score hosts by PCIe locality and NVLink topology; prototype in infra/profiles repo. Owner: Daniel Roth (PR link above).

Open questions
- To what extent cloud provider NIC interrupt steering can be tuned to reduce IRQ coupling? Some host-level knobs exist but need lift/partnering with cloud support.
- For H100 with NVLink, what's the worst-case fragmentation when models exceed NVLink partition? We saw graceful fallback but increased variance — need a targeted fragmentation test.

References / logs
- Raw traces: s3://redwood-perf/rt/pci-topology/2026-02-28/ (private)
- Perf counter snapshots and perf scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/perf-scripts/tree/pci-topology-bench
- JIRA ticket for client report: JIRA-RT-721

Notes to reviewers
- This is an early draft of findings; numbers are medians from limited runs. Treat as operational guidance rather than a final benchmark chart.
- If we decide to act (allocator changes or doc updates), we should run a larger N with locked firmware and an expanded SKU list.

Quick TL;DR (one-liner): placement-group + PCIe locality + NVLink materially reduce tail risk and improve sustained decode throughput for latency-sensitive long-context workloads — pin CPUs and prefer same-root/NVLink hosts where possible.
